scenes.text: This is RELAY. Don't just agree. Understand.
In a study group chat, the fastest person posts the answer. Everyone nods. And three people leave thinking they understood it.
RELAY lives in your Discord server. An admin adds the bot once. Then anyone can start a study session in a channel, with slash relay create.
Friends join with slash relay join. Each person adds when they're free, privately. RELAY proposes one time, and everyone approves that exact version.
The bot posts a link to the web room. Sign in with Discord. RELAY only asks who you are, and shows only the sessions you've joined.
Round one. Think privately. Everyone answers alone, and says how sure they are. Nobody sees anyone else's answer.

Here's the moment RELAY is built for. Three friends agreed, confidently, and they were all wrong. RELAY doesn't follow the majority. It checks the reviewed source, and gives the group one question to talk through.
A friend explains the idea in their own words, and passes the baton. Hints come from a reviewed teaching note. An AI model can draft them too, always labeled, and it never grades anyone.
Think a question is unfair? Anyone can challenge it. The room pauses, the host checks the source, then resumes or discards it. Nobody is marked wrong.
Then a fresh problem. A different scenario, the same idea, answered alone again.
Finally, everyone gets a private receipt. What was checked, what you did, and one honest next step. No scores. No rankings.
Your group explains it. RELAY checks a fresh problem. Try a sample round, right in your browser.
